# A dialog can only animate out of a component, not out of any node

## Context

Found while shaping #21064 (web desktop, #21061): a double-click on a launcher icon should open the app's window animating out of that icon. The launcher is a `list.Base`, so an icon is a list item node, not a component.

## The Problem

`dialog.Base` takes the animation origin as `animateTargetId_` (`{String|null}`), but it resolves that id to a component and reads the window and app from the component:

- `get animateTarget()` returns `Neo.getComponent(this.animateTargetId)` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:156-158`).
- `animateShow()` does `me.windowId = animateTarget.windowId; me.appName = appName = animateTarget.appName` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:420-421`).
- `animateHide()` does the same (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:371-372`).

An id that names a DOM node without a component (a list item, a grid cell, a menu row) leaves `animateTarget` null, and the first line of `animateShow()` throws. The geometry the animation needs comes from `getDomRect(me.animateTargetId)` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:423`), which works for any node. Only the window and app lookups require a component.

A dialog already knows its own `windowId` and `appName` when its creator passes them, which is the documented way to create one (`apps/email/view/ComposeDialog.mjs`; the pattern recorded in #21064).

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: none found (searched `src/dialog/Base.mjs` JSDoc, `learn/` guides on dialogs, `ask_knowledge_base`). `animateTargetId_` is documented as `{String|null}` with no component requirement; `animateTarget` is documented as `{Neo.component.Base|null}`, which the code then dereferences without the null case.

The "assuming that we want to show the dialog inside the same browser window as the animation target" comments (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:370`, `:419`) explain why the target's window is preferred: a component target can live in another browser window. A plain node has no component to ask, so the dialog keeps the window and app it was created with.

## The Fix

- `src/dialog/Base.mjs`: `animateShow()` and `animateHide()` adopt `windowId` and `appName` from `animateTarget` only when it exists, and otherwise keep the dialog's own. The `animateTarget` JSDoc names the null case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dialog whose `animateTargetId` names a DOM node without a component shows and hides with the animation, in its own `windowId` and `appName` (unit test with the main-thread calls stubbed; red on `dev`, green after).
- [ ] A component target keeps today's behavior: the dialog adopts the target's `windowId` and `appName` (existing dialog specs stay green, plus one arm for it).
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` green.

## Out of Scope

- Moving a dialog across browser windows (unchanged; a component target still decides that).
- Any change to the animation itself.
